newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea proposes reform to end labour strife.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea proposes reform to end labour strife.

text.p: South Korea on Tuesday proposed a revision of restrictive labour laws aimed at ending a decade of often violent industrial conflict and improving competitiveness of local companies, the prime minister said.

The proposal lifts the ban on trade unions' political activity, allows outside intervention in labour disputes and removes restrictions barring workers from forming more than one union in each workplace.

Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung said in a statement broadcast on television that providing new labour laws designed to establish new labour-management relations was the "task directly affecting the nation's destiny".
Economists said ending fierce confrontations between unions and managment was the most important issue that needed to be tackled to improve South Korea's economic competitiveness.
The proposed revision allows companies to lay off employees for changes to introduce new technology, improve productivity and end management difficulties.

It also makes clear that workers could no longer claim wages during the period they are on strike. Many South Korean companies have so far paid wages to striking workers to help create better union-management relations.
